people.name: Gonz Sanchez
people.about: Born and raised in Argentina (but half Spanish), lived in Europe (Paris, Milan, Barcelona) and spent significant time in the US (Cincinnati, NYC, SF). I love skiing, reading, coffee, ramen, burgers, boxing, soccer football, architecture, hanging out with my partner and friends, drinking wine and cold weather. I'm a GTM leader with experience scaling brands, teams, and revenue at hyper-growth startups. My last job was VP of Marketing + Growth at On Deck, where I led all things Marketing, Growth and Partnerships through our seed, Series A and Series B, scaling the brand and team from 10 people to over 300 (with 40 under my org). Before that, I was the Head of Growth at Jobbatical where I helped the company pivot from a talent marketplace to an immigration software platform, and led go-to-market/launched in 3 countries simultaneously, going from $100k to $1M ARR in 9 months - in the middle of COVID. After leaving On Deck in mid 2023, I turned Seedtable - a newsletter on EU tech read by 25k founders/investors I've been writing for a while as a side project - into a data platform selling to companies and VCs. Seedtable was acquired in June. I can build the 0 to 1 - I love it, and I think I have good enough taste taste to craft a fantastic consumer experience and a pharma brand/media people and experts love. I can also manage the 1 to 10 and have experience building strong, independent teams that works at a high but sustainable pace to produce quality outcomes. For instance, at On Deck, I've built and led a 40-person org (~10 direct reports, too many if you ask me). I consider myself a GTM-oriented generalist – I spike on Marketing/content but I've built and led Sales, Partnerships and Outbound teams, managed funnels and P&Ls, launched in multiple countries, successfully built motions for different personas in multiple industries, etc. I love being a partner to founders/CEOs. I can context-switch between the tactical day to day - e.g. do IC work to get something through the finish line - and the strategic 12/18-month view.
people.values: Optimism. I aim to be an optimist at a micro (life will be OK) and a macro level (technology will save the world) Honesty. I commit to radical honesty, not for others, but for myself. Honest about who I am, my defects, and how I behave. Default to trust. I chose to trust people (to a reasonable extent) by default, assuming that every now and then I will get burned (but it’ll be a net positive in the long run, even taking into account the times I get burned). Positive sum. Aim to build a bigger pie so everyone can take a bigger piece. The world is, rarely, zero sum. Progressive progress. I aspire to be the best version of myself. I recognize that progress takes time - endurance is the moat - so as long as I’m better today than I was yesterday, I’ll take it.

people.values: Understand the human in front of you - Take the time to understand the person you’re working with, what makes them tick, what are they motivated by, and life experiences that may have impacted their world view. You’ll be 10x more effective. Be transparent and direct, but never disrespectful - Speak with openness, transparency, and say the hard things. People respond better when the message is clear. Be bold and adaptive - Don’t do things just because that’s how they’ve been done before, ask the questions, try to get to the best outcome. And when it doesn’t work, try something else. Get back up - Life has many, many ups and downs. Have your down moments, but get back up. The world needs your magic (cc Dressed in lala  💃).

people.values: Assume good intent - people (especially the people we are working with) generally have good intentions or are trying to have a positive outcome. If we understand, believe that, and remind ourselves of the positive intentions, we can generally reason and get to a solution quicker because we can inherently trust we are working towards the same goals. No question is a dumb question but everyone should use their resources to try and answer questions. Nothing is more annoying than being asked a question that Google can answer. Be mindful of everyones time and ask all the questions that require more insight than the tools at our fingertips. We should all celebrate each others wins. Recruiting is fun and is way more fun when you can celebrate together.

people.name: Shannon Toomey
people.about: I started my career in social work, and ended up working with teens at Boys & Girls Clubs for a few years - I loved the work, but got to a point where the stress was high and the pay was low and it just didn’t feel sustainable anymore, unfortunately. I somehow stumbled into tech and got a contract position at Microsoft doing University Recruiting. I loved how much there was to learn, and the pace, and eventually moved over to SWE Recruiting at Google. From there, I helped grow the Dropbox Seattle office, moved to the Bay, and had a sneaking suspicion I might like startups - and I was right! I knew I didn’t want to specialize in something, I wanted to understand how the pieces fit together. If it’s vague, abstract, maybe a little confusing and people-related, I’m interested. Before Carrara I was at Descript for 5 years, joining as the first Recruiter then growing out a team and eventually overseeing Recruiting and HRBP work. It was a wild ride with some wild characters, and I’m excited to bring my variety of learnings and experiences here - and learn even more! 😊
